name: Bell's Palsy / Acute Peripheral Facial Nerve Palsy
definition: Acute unilateral lower-motor-neuron facial weakness without an identified alternative cause after appropriate assessment.

typical: Altered taste or hyperacusis may occur

redFlags.item: Forehead-sparing weakness or other focal neurological deficits suggesting stroke
Progressive course, systemic illness or tumour concern

investigations.principle: Typical isolated Bell's palsy usually does not require routine imaging.
investigations.MRI: MRI is appropriate for atypical, recurrent, progressive or nonrecovering cases.

green: Urgent eye protection when closure is incomplete
Early evidence-based medical therapy when appropriate
amber: Steroid/antiviral decisions depend on timing, contraindications and diagnostic certainty.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Ardita is a classical correlation often discussed, but modern neurological exclusion of stroke and other causes is mandatory.

patientEducation.summary: Acute unilateral lower-motor-neuron facial weakness without an identified alternative cause after appropriate assessment.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
